$comment: Every distribution in this repository that declares a version nobody can
install, with the reason that state is acceptable. Measured by
`scripts/declared_publication_sweep.py`, guarded by
`tests/architecture/test_declared_publication.py`.
## Why this file exists at all
`test_module_version_sync.py` proves a module's three version surfaces
AGREE. It cannot prove the agreed version EXISTS. `dotmac-integration`
reads 0.1.0a2 on all three surfaces and the version-identity guard passes,
while the newest tag is dotmac-integration-v0.1.0a1 — internal consistency
and publication are different questions, and only the first one had a
guard. A consumer reading the repository, the changelog or
docs/MODULE_CATALOG.md and pinning ==0.1.0a2 gets a resolver error.
## What a row here does and does not mean
A row means the state is KNOWN and someone has said why. It is not
permission to leave it there, and it is emphatically not a reason to edit
the declared version down to match the index: that would make the
repository agree with the registry by discarding the work the number
describes, and the changelog entry for the unpublished version would then
belong to nothing.
The repair is not always a release, either. `dotmac-imports` was reported
as an anomaly BECAUSE it was release-allowlisted with no tag; the ruling
was that the allowlist row was the wrong half, and it was removed rather
than the module published. Two states this file must keep distinct:
* INTENDED — the distribution is meant to be unpublished right now
(`dotmac-auth-oidc`, `dotmac-imports`). The row records the decision so
the next reader does not undo it by dispatching a release.
* OUTSTANDING — a version is genuinely owed to consumers. The row
records evidence a decision still needs. Two worked examples have now
passed through and been removed on release: `dotmac-integration`
0.1.0a2 (released as a3) and `dotmac-kernel` 0.1.0a67. A row that
expires on its own release is the healthiest shape an entry here has.
Both are recorded the same way and neither is a pass. The reason text is
where the difference lives, which is why the guard requires a premise
rather than a label.
## Two directions, both failures
A distribution entering this state without a row fails — that is a version
silently promised to consumers. A row whose distribution has since been
published ALSO fails and must be removed in the same change as the release,
because a ledger that only grows stops describing anything (ADR-0018).
## The oracle is a git tag
The release workflows write a tag only after `verify-registry` has
installed the exact published version from the private index and registered
its manifest, so a tag is this repository's own assertion that a version is
installable — stronger than 'an upload succeeded'. The index is not queried
directly: that needs an authenticated URL, which makes the check
un-runnable at PR time and offline, and a gate that cannot run is not a
gate. The stated cost is that a publication whose tag step failed reads
here as unpublished — which is exactly the state
`recover-module-release.yml` exists to repair, so reporting it is correct.

dotmac-analytics.reason: INTENDED pre-adoption state. The tenant-only declared aggregate evidence and rebuildable projection owner is audit-complete, but its exact bytes have not passed Observe PostgreSQL and wheel validation and ERP has not begun shadow comparison. Keep it unallowlisted and unpublished until those gates and source-writer retirement evidence exist.

dotmac-billing.reason: AWAITING FIRST RELEASE, not missing release metadata. a1 is the first complete dual-plane operational-receivables owner and is intentionally never-published while its focused Starter PR and the Vendor CP/Sub adoption-preparation PRs collect review and CI evidence. Michael authorized draft PR preparation but explicitly did not authorize publishing a release. Remove this row only when the exact dotmac-billing-v0.1.0a1 tag has been produced by the verified module release workflow after separate release authorization; never repair it by editing the declared version down or by publishing before the adopter evidence is reviewable.

dotmac-collections.reason: INTENDED pre-adoption state. a1 is the tenant-only Collections policy and case candidate on the shared a75 foundation. It remains unallowlisted and unpublished until its canonical flush-only persistence writer, concurrency proofs and Sub adoption preparation are complete. Never treat integration as a production authority switch.

dotmac-campaigns.reason: INTENDED UNTIL PRODUCT-FIRST CUTOVER. The audited campaign lifecycle and exact-commit Observer validation are complete, but current Sub authority evidence blocks adoption: Sub pins kernel a50, does not compose its lineage, and records consent, idempotency and outbox as unresolved S7+ owner collisions. ADR-0032 requires those cutovers, then Durable Timers, then Sub as the first campaigns authority. Publishing earlier would create installable parallel owners beside the qualifying source. Remove this row only in the release change that records Sub as the first contract consumer and verifies the exact kernel, timers and campaigns artifacts; do not edit the declared version down.

dotmac-domains.reason: OUTSTANDING first-release proof, not permission to create a second domain owner. a1 is the first provider-neutral registered-domain lifecycle for the Dotmac Cloud candidate and is release-allowlisted so the named Cloud sandbox cutover can eventually pin it. It must remain unpublished until the shared a75 commerce train has landed and become installable, this exact Domains change passes the full Observer PostgreSQL and wheel gates, and a separate release authorization is given. A candidate consumer is not an authority switch. Remove this row only when the exact dotmac-domains-v0.1.0a1 tag has been produced by the verified module release workflow; never edit the declared version down.

dotmac-hosting.reason: OUTSTANDING first-release proof, not permission to create a second hosting owner. a1 is the first provider-neutral hosting-account lifecycle for the Dotmac Cloud candidate and is release-allowlisted so the named Cloud panel-sandbox cutover can eventually pin it. It must remain unpublished until the shared a75 commerce train and the preceding kernel a76/Domains stack have landed and become installable, this exact Hosting change passes the full Observer PostgreSQL and wheel gates, and a separate release authorization is given. A candidate consumer is not an authority switch. dotmac-imports.reason: RULED AND RESOLVED 2026-08-15: intended state, not a defect. The sweep first reported this as an anomaly because the module sat in .github/release-modules.json with no dotmac-imports-v tag in any version. The anomaly was the ALLOWLIST ROW, not the missing tag — the package's own EXTRACTION.toml next_action says to keep it audit-complete and unreleased until a real first adopter is ready, and to publish the exact kernel/imports releases just in time for that cutover. Michael ruled: remove the row, do NOT publish. The row is gone from release-modules.json, release-module.yml and recover-module-release.yml; the package keeps its declared 0.1.0a2, its catalogue entry, its kernel floor and its dossier. It is re-added with ERP's adoption proof (cutover 1, gated behind the E8 Organization-to-Tenant and composed-lineage decision). DO NOT 'fix' this by dispatching a release — unreleased is the decision.
